section: Specifying remote pipelines tasks and step actions using resolvers
job_statement: When building CI/CD pipelines, I want to understand how resolvers retrieve remote pipeline and task definitions, so I can reuse existing pipelines and tasks without copying their definitions.
related_jobs: Configure resolver settings; Specify remote resources using resolvers
desired_outcomes: Minimize time spent understanding resolver concepts; Reduce duplication of pipeline and task definitions; Ensure ability to reuse pipelines and tasks from multiple sources
notes: Main job covering understanding of resolver concepts. Covers Hub Bundles Git HTTP and Cluster resolvers.

section: Specifying a remote pipeline task or step action from a Tekton catalog
job_statement: When creating pipelines, I want to fetch pipeline and task definitions from public catalogs like Artifact Hub or Tekton Hub, so I can leverage community-maintained resources without reinventing solutions.
prerequisites: Understand resolver concepts
related_jobs: Configure hub resolver settings; Specify versioned catalog resources
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to locate and use catalog resources; Reduce risk of using untested custom implementations; Ensure access to community-maintained pipelines and tasks
notes: Main job for using public catalogs. Note: Tekton Hub is deprecated in favor of Artifact Hub.

section: Configuring the hub resolver
job_statement: When setting up hub resolver, I want to configure the default catalog and API endpoint, so I can control which hub my pipelines fetch resources from and optionally use self-hosted instances.
parent_job: Fetch pipeline and task definitions from public catalogs
prerequisites: Have cluster admin permissions; Access to TektonConfig custom resource
related_jobs: Configure other resolvers; Set up self-hosted Tekton Hub or Artifact Hub
desired_outcomes: Minimize configuration complexity; Reduce dependency on public hub instances; Ensure team uses approved catalog sources
notes: Covers configuring default-type (artifact or tekton) catalog names and API endpoints. Self-hosted instances require additional configuration.

section: Specifying a remote pipeline task or step action using the hub resolver
job_statement: When creating pipeline runs or tasks, I want to reference specific catalog resources by name, version, and catalog, so I can use standardized tasks without maintaining local copies.
parent_job: Fetch pipeline and task definitions from public catalogs
prerequisites: Hub resolver configured; Know resource name and version from catalog
related_jobs: Pass additional task parameters; Handle resource versioning
desired_outcomes: Minimize YAML complexity in pipeline definitions; Reduce risk of version drift; Ensure reproducible pipeline executions with pinned versions
notes: Covers pipelineRef taskRef and step.ref with resolver: hub. Includes catalog type kind name and version parameters.

section: Specifying a remote pipeline task or step action from a Tekton bundle
job_statement: When managing pipeline resources, I want to fetch pipeline and task definitions from OCI bundles stored in container registries, so I can version and distribute resources using existing registry infrastructure.
prerequisites: Access to OCI-compatible registry; Understanding of OCI image format
related_jobs: Configure bundles resolver; Publish Tekton bundles to registry
desired_outcomes: Minimize additional infrastructure for resource distribution; Reduce complexity by reusing registry authentication; Ensure resources are versioned alongside container images
notes: Main job for OCI bundle-based distribution. Bundles are OCI images containing Tekton resources.

section: Configuring the bundles resolver
job_statement: When setting up bundles resolver, I want to configure the default service account and resource kind, so I can ensure proper registry authentication and default behaviors.
parent_job: Fetch pipeline and task definitions from OCI bundles
prerequisites: Have cluster admin permissions; Service account with registry credentials configured
related_jobs: Configure registry pull secrets; Set up image pull policies
desired_outcomes: Minimize authentication failures; Reduce need to specify service account in every resource; Ensure consistent registry access across pipelines
notes: Covers default-service-account and default-kind configuration in TektonConfig CR.

section: Specifying a remote pipeline task or step action using the bundles resolver
job_statement: When creating pipeline runs or tasks, I want to reference resources from OCI bundles by fully qualified image name, so I can use privately hosted or organizationally controlled task definitions.
parent_job: Fetch pipeline and task definitions from OCI bundles
prerequisites: Bundles resolver configured; Service account with registry access; Bundle image published to registry
related_jobs: Manage bundle versions; Handle private registry authentication
desired_outcomes: Minimize dependency on public catalogs; Reduce risk of using unvetted external resources; Ensure use of organization-approved task definitions
notes: Covers bundle name kind and serviceAccount parameters. Examples show PipelineRun Pipeline TaskRun and Task with step references.

section: Specifying a remote pipeline task or step action with anonymous Git cloning
job_statement: When fetching resources from Git, I want to use anonymous cloning to retrieve pipeline and task definitions from public repositories, so I can use open-source resources without managing credentials.
prerequisites: Access to public Git repository; Git repository contains YAML pipeline/task definitions
related_jobs: Configure Git resolver for anonymous access; Specify branch and path for resources
desired_outcomes: Minimize credential management overhead; Reduce complexity for public repository access; Ensure ability to reference specific branches or tags
notes: Main job for anonymous Git access. No authentication required for public repos.

section: Configuring the Git resolver for anonymous Git cloning
job_statement: When setting up Git resolver for anonymous access, I want to configure default repository URL, revision, and timeout, so I can simplify resource references and control resolution timing.
parent_job: Fetch resources from Git using anonymous cloning
prerequisites: Have cluster admin permissions; Access to TektonConfig custom resource
related_jobs: Configure Git resolver for authenticated access; Set global timeout policies
desired_outcomes: Minimize repetitive URL specification in pipelines; Reduce resolver timeout issues; Ensure consistent default Git repository for team
notes: Covers default-revision fetch-timeout and default-url configuration. Global 1-minute max timeout applies.

section: Specifying a remote pipeline task or step action by using the Git resolver for anonymous cloning
job_statement: When creating pipeline runs or tasks, I want to reference resources from Git repositories by URL, revision, and path, so I can use version-controlled pipeline definitions without local copies.
parent_job: Fetch resources from Git using anonymous cloning
prerequisites: Git resolver configured; Know repository URL branch/tag and file path
related_jobs: Pin to specific commit SHA; Use branch or tag references
desired_outcomes: Minimize maintenance of local task copies; Reduce risk of outdated task definitions; Ensure reproducibility by referencing specific commits or tags
evidence: remote-pipelines-tasks-resolvers-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Specifying using Git resolver anon lines 610-756
notes: Covers url revision (branch/tag/SHA) and pathInRepo parameters. Cannot use url and repo parameters together.

section: Specifying a remote pipeline task or step action with an authenticated Git API
job_statement: When accessing private Git repositories, I want to use authenticated SCM APIs to fetch pipeline and task definitions, so I can use organization-internal resources securely.
prerequisites: Access to private Git repository; SCM API token with read permissions
related_jobs: Configure authenticated Git resolver; Manage SCM API tokens securely
desired_outcomes: Minimize exposure of internal pipeline definitions; Reduce risk of unauthorized access to private resources; Ensure secure credential management for Git access
notes: Main job for authenticated Git access. Supports GitHub GitLab Gitea Bitbucket.

section: Configuring the Git resolver for an authenticated API
job_statement: When setting up authenticated Git access, I want to configure SCM provider, server URL, and API token secret, so I can enable secure access to private repositories.
parent_job: Access private Git repositories using authenticated SCM APIs
prerequisites: Have cluster admin permissions; Created secret with SCM API token; Access to TektonConfig custom resource
related_jobs: Configure multiple Git providers; Rotate API tokens
desired_outcomes: Minimize token exposure risk; Reduce configuration complexity; Ensure support for enterprise Git instances
notes: Covers scm-type server-url api-token-secret-name api-token-secret-key api-token-secret-namespace and default-org. Supports GitHub GitLab Gitea Bitbucket.

section: Configuring many Git providers
job_statement: When working with multiple Git systems, I want to configure multiple SCM provider configurations with unique keys, so I can access resources from different GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket instances.
parent_job: Access private Git repositories using authenticated SCM APIs
prerequisites: Multiple Git provider instances; API tokens for each provider; Access to TektonConfig custom resource
related_jobs: Select provider configuration in pipeline runs; Manage provider-specific tokens
desired_outcomes: Minimize need to reconfigure resolver for different providers; Reduce complexity of multi-provider environments; Ensure ability to use both public and private Git instances
notes: Uses prefix keys (e.g. test1.scm-type) for multiple configs. Cannot use '.' in configKey values. Default config used if no configKey specified.

section: Specifying a remote pipeline task or step action using the Git resolver with the authenticated SCM API
job_statement: When creating pipeline runs or tasks with private resources, I want to reference Git resources by organization, repository, and path using authenticated APIs, so I can use internal task definitions securely.
parent_job: Access private Git repositories using authenticated SCM APIs
prerequisites: Authenticated Git resolver configured; Access permissions to target repository; Know org repo and file path
related_jobs: Use anonymous Git for public resources; Override resolver configuration per resource
desired_outcomes: Minimize credential management in pipeline definitions; Reduce risk of credential leakage; Ensure access to private organizational resources
evidence: remote-pipelines-tasks-resolvers-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Specifying using Git resolver SCM lines 931-1094
notes: Uses org repo revision pathInRepo parameters. Cannot combine url and repo parameters. Uses authenticated API instead of git clone.

section: Specifying many Git providers
job_statement: When using multiple Git providers, I want to select specific provider configurations by passing configKey parameter, so I can access resources from different Git instances in the same pipeline.
parent_job: Access private Git repositories using authenticated SCM APIs
prerequisites: Multiple Git providers configured; Know configKey for target provider
related_jobs: Configure multiple Git providers; Manage provider selection logic
desired_outcomes: Minimize need to modify resolver configuration; Reduce complexity when accessing multiple Git systems; Ensure correct provider selection for each resource
notes: Pass configKey parameter to select non-default configuration. Value 'default' or omitted uses default config. '.' in configKey not supported.

section: Specifying a remote pipeline or task by using the Git resolver with the authenticated SCM API overriding the Git resolver configuration
job_statement: When accessing Git providers outside default configuration, I want to override resolver settings with inline parameters, so I can access resources from unapproved or ad-hoc Git instances without changing global configuration.
parent_job: Access private Git repositories using authenticated SCM APIs
prerequisites: Access to SCM API token; Know target Git server URL and credentials
related_jobs: Configure default Git resolver; Manage inline credentials securely
desired_outcomes: Minimize delay waiting for global configuration changes; Reduce dependency on platform team for ad-hoc access; Ensure ability to access temporary or test Git instances
notes: Override parameters: token tokenKey scmType serverURL. Use with caution as credentials are in TaskRun/PipelineRun spec.

section: Specifying a remote pipeline task or step action by using the HTTP resolver
job_statement: When fetching resources from HTTP endpoints, I want to retrieve pipeline and task definitions from remote URLs, so I can use resources hosted on web servers or CDNs without Git infrastructure.
prerequisites: Access to HTTP/HTTPS URL hosting YAML file; URL is accessible from cluster
related_jobs: Configure HTTP resolver; Handle URL authentication if needed
desired_outcomes: Minimize dependency on Git or OCI registries; Reduce infrastructure complexity for simple resource hosting; Ensure ability to fetch resources from arbitrary HTTP sources
notes: Main job for HTTP-based resource fetching. URL must point to YAML file defining pipeline task or step action.

section: Configuring the HTTP resolver
job_statement: When setting up HTTP resolver, I want to configure fetch timeout, so I can prevent resolution failures from slow HTTP endpoints.
prerequisites: Have cluster admin permissions; Access to TektonConfig custom resource
related_jobs: Monitor resolver timeout metrics; Tune timeout for network conditions
desired_outcomes: Minimize resolver timeout errors; Reduce impact of slow HTTP servers; Ensure consistent timeout behavior across pipelines
notes: Only configurable parameter is fetch-timeout. Default appears to be 1m based on example.

section: Specifying a remote pipeline task or step action with the HTTP Resolver
job_statement: When creating pipeline runs or tasks, I want to reference resources by HTTP URL, so I can use pipeline definitions hosted on web servers or content delivery networks.
prerequisites: HTTP resolver configured; URL points to valid YAML file; Network access to URL from cluster
related_jobs: Version control HTTP-hosted resources; Handle URL availability
desired_outcomes: Minimize deployment complexity for simple resource hosting; Reduce need for Git or registry infrastructure; Ensure access to centrally hosted pipeline definitions
notes: Single parameter: url (fully qualified HTTP/HTTPS URL). Examples show PipelineRun Pipeline TaskRun and Task with step references.

section: Specifying a pipeline task or step action from the same cluster
job_statement: When reusing resources across namespaces, I want to reference pipeline and task definitions from other namespaces on the same cluster, so I can centralize standard tasks without duplicating definitions.
prerequisites: Resource exists in target namespace; RBAC permissions to access target namespace
related_jobs: Configure cluster resolver; Access standard OpenShift Pipelines tasks
desired_outcomes: Minimize duplication of task definitions across namespaces; Reduce maintenance burden for common tasks; Ensure consistent task versions across projects
notes: Main job for cluster-local resource access. Particularly useful for accessing tasks in openshift-pipelines namespace.

section: Configuring the cluster resolver
job_statement: When setting up cluster resolver, I want to configure default namespace, default kind, and namespace access controls, so I can simplify resource references and enforce security boundaries.
parent_job: Reference resources from other cluster namespaces
prerequisites: Have cluster admin permissions; Access to TektonConfig custom resource
related_jobs: Configure namespace RBAC; Define allowed/blocked namespaces
desired_outcomes: Minimize security risks from cross-namespace access; Reduce configuration in pipeline definitions; Ensure compliance with namespace isolation policies
notes: Covers default-kind default-namespace allowed-namespaces blocked-namespaces. Namespace restrictions provide security controls.

section: Specifying a pipeline task or step action from the same cluster using the cluster resolver
job_statement: When creating pipeline runs or tasks, I want to reference resources by name and namespace within the cluster, so I can use centralized task definitions without local copies.
parent_job: Reference resources from other cluster namespaces
prerequisites: Cluster resolver configured; Target resource exists in specified namespace; RBAC access to target namespace
related_jobs: Access standard tasks from openshift-pipelines namespace; Share tasks across team namespaces
desired_outcomes: Minimize local task duplication; Reduce maintenance overhead; Ensure use of centrally managed task versions
notes: Parameters: name namespace kind (pipeline|task|stepaction). Examples show accessing resources from other namespaces.

section: Tasks provided in the pipelines-shortname namespace
job_statement: When building pipelines, I want to discover and use standard tasks provided by OpenShift Pipelines, so I can leverage pre-built, tested tasks for common operations like building images, cloning Git repos, and running CLI tools.
prerequisites: OpenShift Pipelines installed; Access to openshift-pipelines namespace
related_jobs: Reference tasks using cluster resolver; Understand task parameters and workspaces
desired_outcomes: Minimize time building common pipeline tasks from scratch; Reduce errors by using tested standard tasks; Ensure access to up-to-date task implementations
notes: Reference section covering buildah git-cli git-clone kn kn-apply maven openshift-client s2i-* tasks skopeo-copy tkn opc. Tasks accessed via cluster resolver from openshift-pipelines namespace.

section: Community tasks provided in the pipelines-shortname namespace
job_statement: When integrating with third-party tools, I want to use community-maintained tasks for tools like Argo CD, Helm, Jib, and Jenkins, so I can extend pipelines without writing custom integration logic.
prerequisites: OpenShift Pipelines installed with community tasks; Understanding of target tool (Argo CD Helm etc.)
related_jobs: Reference community tasks using cluster resolver; Configure tool-specific credentials
desired_outcomes: Minimize custom integration development effort; Reduce maintenance of tool-specific pipeline logic; Ensure use of community-tested integrations
notes: Reference section covering argocd-task-sync-and-wait helm-upgrade-from-repo helm-upgrade-from-source jib-maven kubeconfig-creator pull-request trigger-jenkins-job. Accessed via cluster resolver.

section: Step action definitions provided with pipelines-shortname
job_statement: When creating reusable task steps, I want to use standard StepAction definitions like git-clone and cache operations, so I can compose tasks from tested, reusable step actions.
prerequisites: OpenShift Pipelines installed; Understanding of StepAction concept
related_jobs: Reference step actions using cluster resolver; Implement caching strategies
desired_outcomes: Minimize duplication of common step logic; Reduce task complexity through composition; Ensure consistent step implementations across tasks
notes: Covers git-clone StepAction and cache-upload/cache-fetch StepActions (Tech Preview). StepActions are finer-grained than tasks used within task step definitions.

section: About non-versioned and versioned tasks and step actions
job_statement: When choosing between task versions, I want to understand the differences between non-versioned and versioned tasks, so I can decide whether to use stable versioned tasks or auto-updating non-versioned tasks.
prerequisites: OpenShift Pipelines installed; Understanding of operator upgrade process
related_jobs: Plan operator upgrade strategy; Manage task version lifecycle
desired_outcomes: Minimize pipeline breakage from operator upgrades; Reduce risk of missing security updates; Ensure appropriate task versioning strategy for production vs development
notes: Non-versioned tasks auto-update with operator versioned tasks (e.g. buildah-1-18-0) persist across minor versions. Trade-off between stability and updates.
